title: Cinnamon-Sugar Buttermilk Cake Doughnuts
summary: Old-fashioned buttermilk cake doughnuts with nutmeg, fried until crackled and tossed warm in cinnamon sugar.
equipment: stand mixer with paddle (or large bowl and wooden spoon)
8 cm doughnut cutter (or 8 cm and 2.5 cm round cutters)
baking tray lined with floured baking paper
large heavy pan or casserole, at least 24 cm wide
wire rack over a tray lined with kitchen paper

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
neutral frying oil (sunflower, rapeseed or vegetable)

steps.title: Start the dry mix
steps.text: Combine 120 g of the flour with the sugar, baking powder, bicarbonate, nutmeg and salt. Holding back most of the flour lets you beat the batter smooth without overworking the final dough.

steps.title: Whisk the wet mix
steps.text: In a jug, whisk the buttermilk, cooled melted butter, eggs and yolk until evenly combined.

steps.title: Bring the dough together
steps.text: Beat the wet ingredients into the dry on medium speed for 30 seconds until smooth. Add the remaining 360 g flour on low speed and stop the moment it is combined; the dough will be soft and tacky, somewhere between a batter and a cookie dough.

steps.title: Heat the oil
steps.text: Pour oil into the pan to about 4 cm deep, never above half full, and heat to 185 °C. Cake doughnuts need hotter oil than yeast ones so the outside sets quickly and cracks open attractively.

steps.title: Roll and stamp
steps.text: Tip the dough onto a well-floured surface and roll it 1.2 cm thick with a floured pin. Cut out rings, dipping the cutter in flour between cuts, then press the scraps together and cut again to make about 14 rings plus the holes.

steps.title: Fry until cracked
steps.text: Fry 4 at a time for about 60-75 seconds per side, keeping the oil between 180 and 185 °C, until deep golden and split around the edge; the holes need about 1 min in total. Test one first: a cocktail stick pushed into the thickest part should come out clean. Drain on the rack.

steps.title: Coat in cinnamon sugar
steps.text: Mix the sugar and cinnamon in the shallow bowl and toss each doughnut while still warm, so the coating clings to the slightly oily surface. Serve the same day.

tips: Do not skimp on flour when rolling; the soft dough sticks easily, and extra flour on the surface will not toughen it.
A common mistake is overmixing after the last flour goes in, which makes the doughnuts tough and bready.
Keep the oil at 180-185 °C; cooler oil gives pale, greasy doughnuts that do not crack.
Fresh nutmeg gives the classic old-fashioned flavour.
safety: Frying safety: use a heavy, deep pot no more than half full of oil, with a clip-on thermometer, and dry the food before it goes in. Never leave hot oil unattended. If the oil catches fire, turn off the heat and cover the pot with a metal lid or use a fire extinguisher; never use water.
Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Best on the day of frying. Store leftovers in a paper bag at room temperature for up to 1 day, then refresh in a 150 °C oven for 5 min and re-roll in cinnamon sugar.
